subject: science
chapter: Chapter 1 · Water — The Essence of Life
source: NCERT Our Wondrous World (Class V), Chapter 1

topics.name: How much water? Fresh and salt water
Forms of water and the water cycle

levelNotes.easy: Facts from the chapter – who, what, where.
levelNotes.hard: Why and how questions – use what you learnt.
levelNotes.advanced: Think like a scientist: real-life puzzles and tricky reasoning, still from this chapter.

questions.q: Most of the water on Earth is…
questions.e: Most of the Earth’s surface is covered with water, but the majority of it is salty.

questions.q: If all the water on Earth were in a 200 ml glass, how much would be freshwater?
questions.e: The book compares: 200 ml glass of water → only 5 ml (a teaspoon) is freshwater.

questions.q: All living beings — people, animals, birds and plants — depend on which water to survive?
questions.e: Freshwater is needed for drinking, growing crops and daily activities.

questions.q: In the salt pans of Gujarat, what is done with seawater?
questions.a: It is dried to collect salt
w: It is used to water crops
questions.e: The salt pans of Gujarat are one of the largest salt-producing areas in India.

questions.q: Which of these is a freshwater lake in Jammu and Kashmir, one of the largest in Asia?
questions.e: Wular Lake helps regulate river flow to prevent floods.

questions.q: Why can’t we drink ocean water?
w: It has no water in it
questions.e: Ocean water is salt water, so it is not fit for drinking.

questions.q: ‘Johads’ in Rajasthan are…
questions.a: small earthen dams built to collect rainwater and recharge groundwater
questions.e: Johads are a traditional way of saving rainwater.

questions.q: Is {x} freshwater or salt water?
pairs: sea water in the salt pans
questions.e: {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: Is {x} freshwater or salt water?
pairs: sea water in the salt pans
questions.e: {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: Ice is the ___ form of water.
questions.e: Water has three forms: solid (ice), liquid (rain) and vapour (steam).

questions.q: Steam is the ___ form of water.
questions.e: When water is heated it turns into water vapour (steam).

questions.q: Which form of water is {x}?
questions.e: {x} is the {ans} form of water.

questions.q: Which form of water is {x}?
questions.e: {x} is the {ans} form of water.

questions.q: The constant circular movement of water in nature is called the…
questions.e: Water evaporates, forms clouds, falls as rain, snow or hail and returns to rivers, lakes and oceans.

questions.q: In Activity 2, water droplets form on the outside of a steel glass with ice. Where do they come from?
questions.a: Water vapour in the air cools and turns into droplets
w: The ice jumps out of the glass
The droplets come from the table
questions.e: Yes – there is water in the air too (water vapour). It cools on the cold glass.

questions.q: What causes water in oceans and rivers to turn into water vapour?
questions.e: Heat changes water into vapour; when vapour cools it forms droplets and clouds.

questions.q: In the water-cycle bag activity, what happens when the water vapour inside the bag cools?
questions.a: It forms small droplets that fall back down
questions.e: This is just like clouds giving rain in nature.

questions.q: Clouds come down to Earth as…
questions.e: Water vapour forms clouds which come down as rain, snow and hail.

questions.q: Water that gets stored deep under the ground is called…
questions.e: Rainwater soaks into the soil and sinks through layers of soil and rocks.

questions.q: Which of these do we use to draw groundwater?
questions.a: Wells, borewells, tube wells and handpumps
questions.e: These bring groundwater up for our use.

questions.q: Rivers, ponds and lakes are examples of…
questions.e: They are natural sources of freshwater on the surface.

questions.q: Why is groundwater not recharged easily in cities?
questions.a: Cemented surfaces stop rainwater from going into the ground
w: It does not rain in cities
questions.e: Open, uncovered areas let water seep in.

questions.q: Which surface helps groundwater recharge the most?
questions.e: Water can soak into the soil of a lawn.

questions.q: In the mustard seed activity, how do the seeds move on the crumpled paper?
questions.a: Down the slopes, spreading and collecting in low places
questions.e: Like water, they flow from higher to lower ground and follow the shape of the land.

questions.q: Rivers in India flow into the Bay of Bengal or the…
questions.e: Some rivers flow east to the Bay of Bengal, some west to the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: Which major Indian river does NOT drain into a sea?
questions.e: The Luni starts in the Aravalli Range and ends in the marshy Rann of Kutch.

questions.q: Hiware Bazar in Maharashtra is an example of a…
questions.e: Local people worked on watershed management and rainwater harvesting.

questions.q: Which animal has fins to swim?
questions.e: Animals in water have features like fins to swim.

questions.q: Why do lotus leaves not get soaked in water?
questions.a: They have a waxy coating that makes them waterproof
questions.e: Activity 9 – a crayon-coated paper also makes water drops roll off.

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao in Manipur is the only floating national park in the world. It is famous for the…
questions.e: It has floating islands called phumdis.

questions.q: The fishing cat is an excellent swimmer because it has…
questions.e: It lives in India’s wetlands and dives for fish.

questions.q: Why do a large number of living beings live near water bodies?
questions.a: They depend on water for drinking, food and shelter
questions.e: Freshwater habitats support rich plant and animal life.

questions.q: True or false? A water lily is a rooted floating plant.
questions.e: Its flowers float on the water but its roots stay in the pond bed.

questions.q: A 200 ml glass stands for all the water on Earth and 5 ml of it is freshwater. What part of the water is freshwater?
questions.e: 200 ÷ 5 = 40, so freshwater is only 1 part in 40 – that is why we must save it.

questions.q: Put the water cycle in the right order starting from the sea.
questions.a: Heat → water vapour → clouds → rain → rivers → sea
questions.e: The Sun heats water, vapour forms clouds, clouds give rain, rain flows back through rivers to the sea.

questions.q: A city is short of groundwater. Which plan will help most?
questions.a: Leave open spaces, build soak pits and plant more trees
questions.e: Water must be able to seep back underground to recharge it.

questions.q: It has not rained in a village for two years. What is most likely to happen?
questions.a: Wells and ponds dry up and people struggle for water
questions.e: Without rain, surface water and groundwater are not refilled.

questions.q: In a river food chain, what would happen if all the fish disappeared?
questions.a: Animals that eat fish, like birds, otters and crocodiles, would go hungry
questions.e: Living beings depend on each other for food (Activity 10).

questions.q: Rainwater falls in a forest and in a city. Where does more of it soak into the ground?
questions.a: In the forest – soil and trees slow the water down
w: In the city – roads soak water
questions.e: Cemented city surfaces send water running off instead of into the ground.

questions.q: Why is it important to save freshwater even though Earth is covered with water?
questions.a: Only a tiny part of Earth’s water is fresh and usable
w: Ocean water is fine to drink
questions.e: Remember the glass and the teaspoon.

questions.q: What can ocean water be used for?
questions.a: Getting salt, and as a home for sea animals
questions.e: Salt pans of Gujarat dry seawater to collect salt.

questions.q: True or false? Water can change into ice and steam, and can also return to its liquid form.
questions.e: The experiments showed water changing form and changing back.
